summary: Harness, auditor, negative tests and native evidence are internally consistent and support the four-case cold FFB matrix: exact 50000 reads/10000 events per case, correct byte totals (335571760000 raw, 33582000000 sim10), FIFO ring of depth 35 that only reuses a slot after future.get and drains pending futures on failure, kernel-free standalone KvikIO timed path with CUDA sync inside the window, 105 post-timing GPU/CPU 64-byte witnesses over all 35 slots, zero resident pages for all five files before every loop, NIC brackets that enclose the loop interval, idle counters, full-file raw SHA and sim10 copy SHA verified before timing, same job/node/GPU/CPU set/settings, filesystem source drpsrcf/ffb for both inputs, and FFB temporary directory removed. All README table values recompute from the JSON. The remaining issues are report-completeness gaps against the agreed acceptance list: the README states the 128 GiB request but does not disclose the measured asymmetry it causes (raw loops run under cgroup page-cache reclaim with ~38-40% final residency while sim10 fits fully, 99.997%), and does not attribute repeat variability to shared/changing storage load or note that both inputs were fully read by this client minutes before timing so server-side cache state is uncontrolled. These are documentation changes; no harness re-run is required.

findings.evidence: README says only 'Exclusive node,128GiB requested memory.' Evidence shows the raw payload (312.5 GiB) exceeds the 128G cgroup, so final_cache residency after each raw loop is 38.1-39.8% (e.g. 00-raw.json s005 resident_pages 5892780/15365395), while sim10 (31.3 GiB) ends at 99.997% resident (01-sim10.json 1281066/1281098). Raw loops therefore run under continuous page-cache reclaim pressure that the sim10 loops never experience; the agreed acceptance list requires the 128 GiB uncertainty to be kept visible.
findings.requested_change: Add a sentence to the README (storage/settings or caveats section) stating that the raw payload exceeds the 128 GiB memory request so the raw loops read under cgroup page-cache reclaim (final residency ~38-40%) whereas sim10 fits entirely (~100%), and that this is an uncontrolled asymmetry of the comparison, not a matched condition.

findings.evidence: README attributes raw variability (3.24 vs 4.16 GiB/s) only to 'meaningful variability' and says generically that client eviction 'does not evict Weka server/storage caches'. It does not state that both inputs were fully read by this client minutes before timing (raw via full-file SHA, sim10 via copy+SHA with the writecache mount option), that the second raw repeat followed the first by ~2 minutes, or that shared FFB load from other users is uncontrolled. The acceptance list asks for 'changing storage load' to remain visible.
findings.requested_change: Extend the caveat to say: server-side Weka cache state was uncontrolled and likely non-cold for both inputs because every byte was hashed/copied through this client shortly before timing; concurrent FFB load from other jobs was not measured; repeat differences cannot be separated from these effects.
